purpose: PR #188 addresses audit issue #187 (PWA offline) by preventing authenticated /api/v1/* data from entering the runtime cache (NetworkOnly allowlist), adding an offline fallback with destination-aware retry, an image placeholder, and a hardened connectivity probe, and stabilizing push-subscription behavior. It also removes the generated sw.js from source control and purges runtime caches on logout.
riskRationale: All 12 previously reported minor issues are resolved, but two important push-subscription gaps remain: subscribe() still unconditionally unsubscribes/re-subscribes on each full page load (recreating churn per load instead of per render), and the LOGOUT handler purges caches but leaves the device's push subscription active and server-registered, so a signed-out account can keep receiving notifications on a shared device. Both are surgical, low-risk autofixes that do not break core functionality.

text: A high-quality, well-scoped frontend-only PWA/offline hardening pass. All 12 previously reported minor findings are resolved at their root causes: health-endpoint allowlist coverage, waitUntil-wrapped message handlers, controller-null logout fallback, a real fetch probe with res.ok + two-consecutive-failure threshold and recovery toast, and the generated sw.js removed from source control. What remains is the push-subscription story: the churn fix is only partial (fixed per-render, not per-page-load) and logout does not unsubscribe the device from push. Both are safely auto-fixable; nothing blocks core functionality.

reasoning: The central push-subscription churn finding is only partially fixed — useCallback plus the ref guard stops within-render re-firing, but the guard resets on every full page load and subscribe() still unconditionally unsubscribes before re-subscribing — and the LOGOUT handler purges caches but leaves the device's push subscription active and server-registered. Add subscription reuse in subscribe() and pushManager cleanup in the LOGOUT handler, then ship.

message: Inverting the API cache policy to a safe-by-default NetworkOnly allowlist for all /api/v1/* GET requests (instead of the former denylist) closes the authenticated-data leak comprehensively, including /api/v1/health and future endpoints, while still letting the health probe and VAPID key fetch hit the network.

The connectivity probe reads res.ok (not just fetch rejection), requires two consecutive failures to show the offline banner, gates on navigator.onLine and document visibility, and is protected by an inFlight guard plus a genuine offline->online recovery toast — all edge cases from the previous review are handled.

The LOGOUT cache purge correctly falls back to registration.active?.postMessage when navigator.serviceWorker.controller is null (first-load / waiting-SW case), and the name-based precache exclusion protects the app shell while purging all runtime caches.

The document-destination fallback matcher, with a comment tracing how Next.js App Router RSC fetches reach it via MPA fallback, is a well-reasoned, correctly-scoped solution that avoids corrupting the router with an HTML body on RSC requests.

The audit's central 'push-subscription churn' concern is only partially fixed. useCallback + the PushSubscriber ref guard stop within-render re-firing, but the ref guard resets on every full page load (new tab / hard refresh), and subscribe() still unconditionally runs existing.unsubscribe() before re-subscribing. Each fresh load therefore unsubscribes the browser's valid endpoint, subscribes to a brand-new one, and new-upserts a DB row; the old row is orphaned until the next broadcast prunes it via the send-failure deleteMany. This recreates the churn the PR claims to have resolved, just per load instead of per render.
suggestion: Reuse the existing browser subscription when it is still valid and its applicationServerKey matches the advertised VAPID key, only unsubscribing/re-subscribing when they differ or the backing send is known-stale. Normalize both keys to base64url before comparing.

message: The LOGOUT handler purges all non-precache caches but never unsubscribes the device's push subscription. After sign-out, the browser keeps an active pushManager subscription that is still registered server-side, so notifications for the signed-out account keep arriving on the (possibly now shared) device and 'notificationclick' opens their links — exposing the previous account's content to whoever uses the device next. The backend also retains a dead endpoint. Sign-out cleanup is explicitly part of this PR's scope ('Cleared cached data when signing out'), so this is a gap in the new code.
suggestion: Unsubscribe the push subscription in the LOGOUT handler (and, in the client logout() path, notify the backend via /notifications/unsubscribe before redirecting) so sign-out fully clears account-bound device data.
suggestionCode:
const sub = await self.registration.pushManager.getSubscription();
      if (sub) await sub.unsubscribe();

message: GET_INTENDED_DESTINATION reads the recorded failed-navigation URL but never deletes the cache entry, so it persists across sessions in Cache Storage. If /offline is later opened directly (bookmark, refresh, or a fresh offline session where no new destination was recorded), 'Try again' routes to a stale URL from a previous session; the recorded URL can also contain sensitive query parameters (e.g. ?token=...) that linger between sessions until logout purges them.
suggestion: Delete the entry after it is read in the GET_INTENDED_DESTINATION handler (the destination only needs to survive from the failed navigation to the /offline page render), so each failed navigation records a fresh value and stale destinations don't linger.
suggestionCode:
const url = match ? await match.text() : '';
          await cache.delete(INTENDED_DESTINATION_URL);

message: The intended destination is fetched asynchronously via GET_INTENDED_DESTINATION, but the 'Try again' button is interactive immediately. If the user clicks before the SW round-trip resolves (e.g. on a SW cold start), intendedDestination is still null and the handler silently falls back to router.back() instead of the page they actually tapped — the feature is best-effort under a small race.
suggestion: Hold the button disabled (or show a subtle 'reconnecting…' state) until intendedDestination has been resolved or the request has definitively timed out, so a fast click does not dispatch a back-navigation.

message: The probe success path sets isOnline(true) — and can emit the recovery toast — without re-checking navigator.onLine or document.visibilityState. An in-flight probe that resolves after the browser fires 'offline' mid-request (or after the tab is hidden) can flip the UI to 'online' while the browser still reports offline.
suggestion: Before marking online, re-verify navigator.onLine and document.visibilityState === 'visible' (in addition to the existing !cancelled check) so a stale in-flight success cannot override the browser's offline state.
